implementation_risks_for_independent_pre: The finite product model and piChartedSpace are present. The searched general ContMDiff finite-manifold-product construction API is incomplete or not directly named; establish any required chartwise product smoothness internally, without adding an IsManifold/smoothness hypothesis to the source.
The exact implicit models/ENorms are not compiler-verified yet. The proposed types must be elaborated only after independent source/signature acceptance.
Check n=0 and N=0 branches explicitly; annular radial weight is chi(r)/r*r^n, not an unjustified truncated power r^(n-1).
Weighted-gradient regularity must be joint in the full configuration, not merely separately differentiable in each coordinate.

off_source_semantics_audit.ambient_extension: No global ambient extension appears as an input. If an implementation starts with such a theorem, source fulfillment still requires deriving a suitable extension from the intrinsic data.
off_source_semantics_audit.coordinate_chart_semantics: Stereographic/product charts and their induced tangent differential must be identified explicitly; a named operator alone is insufficient.
off_source_semantics_audit.probability_normalization: Both surface mass and its inverse are fixed by definitions, not unconstrained constants.
off_source_semantics_audit.tangency_for_intrinsic_divergence: Intrinsic-divergence interpretation requires the existing pointwise hTangent premise. For W(x)=x on a positive-dimensional unit sphere, the radial-extension ambient trace is n while the tangent projection is zero; the definition is therefore not an intrinsic-divergence operator on arbitrary ambient-valued fields.
off_source_semantics_audit.total_derivative_convention: Mathlib gradient/fderiv are total functions. Under the intrinsic hypotheses, differentiability at every sphere point must be established before their use.
off_source_semantics_audit.zero_branch_at_origin: Not observable by sphere-local derivatives. Must prove eventual agreement on a nonzero neighborhood before using fderiv; never use the default zero derivative to manufacture an identity.
